original_question: If X is a smooth projective variety with pseudo-effective tangent bundle and phi: X -> Y is its holomorphic MRC fibration, must phi be locally trivial?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 4.3: the paper asks whether, for a smooth projective variety with pseudo-effective tangent bundle, the holomorphic MRC fibration is locally trivial. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right open problem very closely: it has the correct ambient class of varieties (smooth projective), the correct positivity hypothesis (pseudo-effective tangent bundle), the correct fibration (a holomorphic MRC fibration), and the exact property being asked about (local triviality). It also matches the surrounding context in which Theorem 4.2 gives a holomorphic smooth MRC fibration, while local triviality is only known under the stronger assumption that T_X is positively curved. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))
missing_details: The paper is working in the complex-analytic/algebraic setting: X is a smooth complex projective variety (projective manifold). ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))

The phrase pseudo-effective tangent bundle refers to the paper's specific notion from Proposition 4.1; a stand-alone version should specify an equivalent condition, for example that there exists an ample line bundle A on X such that A⊗Sym^m(T_X) is generated by global sections at a general point for every integer m>=1. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))

MRC fibrations are only defined up to birational modification of the base Y, so a stand-alone question should indicate that φ is a holomorphic representative of the MRC fibration of X, with Y chosen smooth projective. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))

If MRC fibration is not taken as known notation, it should be defined: an almost holomorphic map with rationally connected general fibers and no horizontal rational curve through a very general point; when the base is smooth, this means the base is not uniruled. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))

The nearby context already supplies that such a holomorphic MRC fibration exists and is smooth for varieties with pseudo-effective tangent bundle; the open problem is whether this smooth morphism is actually locally trivial. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))

Locally trivial should be made explicit as holomorphically locally a product over small analytic open sets of Y; the paper gives this local-product meaning elsewhere when discussing local triviality. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))

The paragraph introducing Problem 4.3 explains why the question is subtle: pseudo-effectivity need not force the tangent bundle to split as T_X ≅ T_{X/Y} ⊕ φ^*T_Y, unlike the nef or positively curved situations, yet no counterexample to local triviality is known. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))
refined_question: Let X be a smooth complex projective variety such that its tangent bundle T_X is pseudo-effective in the sense of Proposition 4.1; equivalently, there exists an ample line bundle A on X for which A⊗Sym^m(T_X) is generated by global sections at a general point for every integer m>=1. Let φ:X→Y be a holomorphic representative of the maximal rationally connected fibration of X, whose existence with Y smooth projective and φ smooth is provided by Theorem 4.2. Must φ be locally trivial as a holomorphic fibration; that is, after shrinking to sufficiently small analytic open sets U⊂Y, is φ^{-1}(U) isomorphic over U to U×F, where F is the fiber? ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))
justification: The closest official formulation is exactly Problem 4.3 in Section 4, not a broader neighboring problem. Section 4 first fixes the paper's notion of pseudo-effectivity via Proposition 4.1, then Theorem 4.2 states that such an X admits a holomorphic MRC fibration φ:X→Y with Y smooth projective and φ smooth. The paragraph immediately after Theorem 4.2 then explains that, unlike the nef tangent bundle case, the tangent bundle need not split, cites a projective-bundle example over an elliptic curve where splitting fails, and explicitly asks whether φ is nevertheless locally trivial. This is therefore the precise paper-faithful sharpening of your draft. ([numdam.org](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/afst.1712.pdf))
